atomic_claims.claim_text: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker and darker.

evidence.passage_text: We’ve debunked the myth that shaving makes hair grow back thicker and darker. The truth is that shaving does not alter the structure of your hair or its growth pattern. By understanding the science behind hair growth, you can confidently choose the hair removal method that best suits your needs.
evidence.source_title: Does Shaving Make Your Hair Grow Back Thicker and Darker? - The Skin Company

evidence.passage_text: One of the most insidious myths out there is the notion that shaving makes your hair grow faster, thicker, or darker. But guess what? It’s just a myth! Hair growth is regulated by genes and hormones, not the razor used to shave with. So shave on with confidence, knowing you’re not altering the essence of your hair—only its form. The shaving hair growth is finally put to rest, and it’s time to look beyond this old wives’ tale.
evidence.source_title: Shaving Hair Growth Myth – Thick Hair Fact or Fiction?

evidence.passage_text: Along with "you don't need to exfoliate your body" and "acne is caused by bad hygiene", the idea that shaving makes your hair grow back thicker, darker or faster is one of those persistent beauty myths that won't seem to quit. If you've ever been in two minds about picking up a razor due to thoughts of prickly stubble, a change in hair colour or overnight regrowth, this article is for you. We're here to clear things up once and for all.
evidence.source_title: Does Shaving Make Hair Grow Back Thicker, Darker or Faster?

evidence.passage_text: “ Is it true that shaving unwanted body hair makes it grow back thicker and darker? “. Mayoclinic.org
evidence.source_title: Shaving Hair Affects Hair Color or Growth - Fact or Myth?

evidence.passage_text: If shaving or cutting hair could cause it to grown back thicker or darker, nobody would be bald unless they wanted to be. The only reason that we sometimes think that shaving or cutting hair makes it grow back thicker of darker is because people tend to jump to conclusions based on what they expect to see. People also tend to observe coincidences and assume a causal relationship where there is none.
evidence.source_title: Shaving Hair Affects Hair Color or Growth - Fact or Myth?

evidence.passage_text: This question has been studied for nearly a century. Anatomist Mildred Trotter published research on shaving and hair growth as early as 1928, specifically targeting the beard, which was (and still is) the area most commonly believed to grow back thicker and darker after shaving. Her work found no such effect, and every controlled study since has reached the same conclusion.
evidence.source_title: Does Shaving Make Hair Darker? What Science Says

evidence.passage_text: To understand why shaving doesn’t make hair grow back thicker or darker, we must look at the science behind hair growth. Hair grows from follicles located beneath the skin’s surface. These follicles determine your hair’s color, thickness, and overall structure. When you shave, you only remove the hair above the skin’s surface, leaving the follicle—and its characteristics—intact.
evidence.source_title: Does Shaving Make Your Hair Grow Back Thicker and Darker? - The Skin Company

evidence.passage_text: Across different cultures, shaving the head is often associated with renewal and rejuvenation. In some traditions, it is believed that removing hair allows for healthier, more robust growth. Many parents shave their child’s head, thinking it will result in thicker, darker strands, a practice prevalent in parts of India, China, and the Middle East. Similarly, men undergoing military training frequently notice a different texture when their hair begins to grow back after a full shave, reinforcing the assumption that shaving influences thickness.
evidence.source_title: Does shaving hair make it thicker? Myth vs. Science Explained

evidence.passage_text: You've probably heard that shaving hair makes it grow back thicker. It's something many of us get told as kids, and end up believing for our whole lives. But is there any evidence for this claim? And if it's not true, why is it so commonly believed? Let's take a look at the truth of how shaving affects your hair growth.
evidence.source_title: Hair Growth After Shaving: Separating Myth from Fact

evidence.passage_text: Shaving cuts off the soft, pointed tips of hair, leaving flat ends that feel thicker and look darker. You notice this that most in areas like legs or faces where hair thickens can change.
evidence.source_title: Shaving Hair Growth Myth – Thick Hair Fact or Fiction?
